episode_title: The 3 Types of Content Every Business Should Post

real_qa.q: What are the three types of content every business should post according to The Social Collective framework?
real_qa.r: The framework is called Seen, Trusted, and Wanted. Seen content establishes your identity, focus, and belief to help people recognize you. Trusted content builds credibility through your method, proof, and the experience of working with you. Wanted content includes calls to action, invitations, and opportunities for people to purchase products or book services.
real_qa.requete: three types content business should post

real_qa.q: What is The Social Collective's signature Seen, Trusted, and Wanted framework and why is it effective?
real_qa.r: The framework operates off the same structure as top, middle, and bottom of funnel content. Seen gets people to know about you through identity, focus, and belief. Trusted deepens connection through method, proof, and experience. Wanted provides calls to action and invitations to purchase or book services. This framework works on basically every brand under the sun.
real_qa.requete: Seen Trusted Wanted framework Social Collective

real_qa.q: How does The Social Collective's Seen content help establish brand identity and cut through marketing noise?
real_qa.r: Seen content focuses on three areas: identity (who you are and what you offer), focus (niching down to a specific audience so you speak to someone rather than everyone), and belief (sharing personal stances and what you stand for as a company). When you get granular with who you support, people reading your content feel you are actually there for them, helping you stand out to people who will connect with you.
real_qa.requete: Seen content identity focus belief marketing

real_qa.q: What types of proof can demonstrate credibility beyond client testimonials and financial screenshots?
real_qa.r: Proof comes in many shapes and forms. It includes your stats, numbers, and data showing you are great at what you do, but also includes showcasing that you are out there doing the thing—such as speaking on stages, sharing knowledge, and becoming a known figure in your industry. Proof demonstrates both your expertise and your active presence in your field.

real_qa.q: How should businesses describe their client experience in trust-building content?
real_qa.r: Share what it looks like to work with you by detailing the experience through emails and social content. When sending a proposal, give a full breakdown of what the first four to six weeks working with you looks like so people understand exactly what the experience will be. This helps people feel supported, guided, and know the direction they are moving in, putting them in a better position to decide if you are right for them.
